extracted.intended_audience: EU policymakers, pharmaceutical industry stakeholders, and IP/legal teams (innovator and generic/biosimilar manufacturers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and position on the European Commission proposal to introduce a manufacturing waiver to the SPC Regulation (469/2009), specifying the conditions, safeguards and implementation details EFPIA believes are required. Focused on how the waiver should be defined, notified, limited and enforced to preserve IP incentives and prevent diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and purpose of SPCs
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the SPC was to offset some of the effective patent term lost during the development of a medicine; the SPC Regulation provides companies that research and develop new medicines the certainty that if a medicine makes it to the market, it will be protected from unfair competition for a limited period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPCs are described as foundational for pharmaceutical incentives that enable investment in long, risky, and costly development; any amendment (e.g., a waiver) should recognise SPCs' role in incentivising innovation and avoid eroding that incentive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver scope — exclusive purpose of export
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'making' is for exclusive purpose of export to third countries where protection for the product or medicinal product does not exist or has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The waiver must be tightly limited to manufacture destined exclusively for non-EU markets without applicable protection; this limitation is central to providing legal certainty and avoiding unintended domestic market impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notification to authorities (and rights holders)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic or biosimilar manufacturer must inform the relevant authority of their intention to seek the benefit of the waiver 28 days in advance (EFPIA proposes extending the timeframe to 3 months); the right holder should also be notified (and not just the relevant authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFPIA supports ex-ante transparency and proposes strengthening the Commission's proposed 28-day notice to a 3-month notice to give both parties sufficient legal certainty. Notification should not be merely indicative but comprehensive (see notification content criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification content — exhaustive list of export markets and earliest date
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification should include an exhaustive, rather than indicative, list of markets to which the generic or biosimilar manufacturer intends to export as well as the earliest date of 'making'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full details so authorities and right holders can assess whether the export destinations are outside protection and to monitor compliance; indicative/partial lists are insufficient for legal certainty and anti-diversion controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging measures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The maker must have taken appropriate packaging measures as a condition for applying the waiver (as per the Commission proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFPIA accepts packaging measures in principle but considers the concept needs clarification and strengthening to be effective in preventing diversion back into the EU market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing contractors of waiver conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The maker must have informed any of its contractors of the conditions of the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties in the supply/manufacturing chain must be made aware of the waiver conditions to ensure compliance and reduce risk of inadvertent or deliberate diversion; this is part of the proposed safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑retrospective implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The waiver should only apply to SPCs applied for on or after the implementation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting application to post‑implementation SPCs preserves legitimate expectations of innovators and supports harmonised implementation across the EU; avoids retroactive weakening of IP rights that influenced past investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑diversion measures — prohibition on re‑import and market placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Products made under the SPC waiver must not be re‑imported into the EU or put on the EU market before SPC expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures must effectively prevent diversion; EFPIA notes simple labelling (a logo) can be easily circumvented and seeks stronger technical solutions (see EMVS/unique identifier criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EMVS / unique identifier as effective anti‑diversion control
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure an easy, workable and effective solution, EFPIA proposes relying on the European Medicines Verification System (EMVS) by requiring that the unique identifier (mandatory for any medicine to be dispensed in the EU) cannot be placed on the product intended for export under the manufacturing waiver before the expiry of the SPC in the EU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFPIA argues EMVS is preferable to a simple outward-facing logo because it leverages an existing system mandated by the Falsified Medicines Directive and is harder to circumvent; implementation detail: prevent placement of the unique identifier on exported packs until after SPC expiry in EU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and legal certainty of waiver conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final legislative text must provide for clarity and certainty on what the waiver entails and under which conditions it applies to ensure that there is no further erosion of essential innovators' IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EFPIA stresses that ambiguous or weakly specified safeguards will undermine the waiver's acceptability and could signal to investors that Europe is weakening its commitment to IP incentives; the text should therefore be precise on definitions, procedures, and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of genuine impact on generic access and healthcare systems
rubrics_metrics.description: EFPIA's position that the SPC manufacturing waiver will not provide for better generic access as generics and biosimilars are often available immediately after SPC expiry and other factors (pricing, reimbursement, market size) affect generic launch delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should assess whether the waiver meaningfully improves patient access or whether it primarily reduces IP protections without delivering proportional access benefits; economic and market studies should inform the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve IP incentives to maintain R&D investment
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal reduces IP rights and sends a signal to the world that Europe is weakening its commitment to intellectual property (IP) incentives and innovation, which puts at risk long‑term investment in jobs, economic growth and advancement of patient care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reform must balance access goals with the need to sustain a predictable IP framework that continues to attract life science investment and supports industrial development; avoid measures that unintentionally devalue IP protections.
